page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.medium is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by a 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor with Neoverse-N1 cores. The hardware configuration delivers 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is sized at 2.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. In addition to general compute resources, this instance includes 59 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD local instance storage. Cryptographic workload acceleration is supported through hardware AES extensions, while no graphics processing units are present.

Benchmark testing reflects the constraints of a single-core Graviton2 allocation. In synthetic processor evaluations, the c6gd.medium achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1,490.59, matching its multi-core result of 1,490.59 due to the single-thread execution profile. Geekbench results produced 917.0 in single-core and 931.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside 1,124.0 in Clang compilation testing. Memory bandwidth achieved 59.39 GB/s for small cached reads, falling to 20.1 GB/s for large uncached reads and 9.8 GB/s for large sequential writes. Application workloads demonstrated throughput of 1.19 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 1.14 GB/s.

The primary operational tradeoff of the c6gd.medium centers on its single-core boundary and limited 2.0 GB memory ceiling, which restrict concurrent multi-threaded execution and large memory-resident datasets. However, pairing dedicated compute with bundled 59 GB NVMe storage provides localized, high-speed input/output without requiring network-attached storage volumes. This instance configuration is suitable for lightweight containerized microservices, modest in-memory caching nodes, ARM64 build agents, and continuous integration tasks that leverage local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.medium is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor core on the Nitro system architecture. The server provides 1 vCPU, 2.0 GB of memory, and 59 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking a discrete GPU, the processor features 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware-level AES cryptographic support. Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate single-threaded capability, achieving 1,490.59 in stress-ng tests and 1.19 million Redis SET operations per second, with overall parallel capacity bounded by its single-core configuration. The integration of fast local NVMe scratch storage with efficient dedicated Arm compute makes this instance type practical for lightweight web services, small caching layers, ARM64 software compilation, and automated testing environments.
